Background

In the data folder, you will find data about shark incidents in California between 1950-2022. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

Load the libraries

library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")

Load the data

Run the following code chunk to import the data. In this chunk, I am removing NA’s.

sharks <- 
  read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv", 
           na=c("NA", "N/A", "Unknown", "NOT COUNTED", "", " ")) %>% 
  clean_names()

Questions

  1. Are there any “hotspots” for shark incidents in California? Show the top five counties with the most incidents.
sharks %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  summarize(number_incidents=n()) %>% 
  arrange(desc(number_incidents))
## # A tibble: 22 × 2
##    county          number_incidents
##    <chr>                      <int>
##  1 San Diego                     25
##  2 Humboldt                      20
##  3 San Mateo                     19
##  4 Santa Barbara                 19
##  5 Marin                         16
##  6 Monterey                      16
##  7 Santa Cruz                    15
##  8 Sonoma                        15
##  9 San Luis Obispo               14
## 10 Los Angeles                   10
## # ℹ 12 more rows
sharks %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  count(county) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n))
## # A tibble: 22 × 2
## # Groups:   county [22]
##    county              n
##    <chr>           <int>
##  1 San Diego          25
##  2 Humboldt           20
##  3 San Mateo          19
##  4 Santa Barbara      19
##  5 Marin              16
##  6 Monterey           16
##  7 Santa Cruz         15
##  8 Sonoma             15
##  9 San Luis Obispo    14
## 10 Los Angeles        10
## # ℹ 12 more rows
  1. Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents per county.
sharks %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  summarize(number_incidents=n()) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=county, y=number_incidents))+
  geom_col(aes(fill=county))+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title="Total number of incidents per county", y="Total number of incidents")

  1. Are there months of the year when incidents are more likely to occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by month. Which month has the highest number of incidents?
sharks <- sharks %>% 
  mutate(across(c(month, day, year), as.factor))
sharks %>% 
  group_by(month) %>% 
  summarize(number_incidents=n()) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=month, y=number_incidents))+
  geom_col(aes(fill=month))+
  labs(title="Total number of incidents by month")+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(size=rel(1.5), hjust=.5))

  1. Is there a time of day when most attacks occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by time of day. Which time of day has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  group_by(day) %>% 
  summarize(number_incidents=n()) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=day, y=number_incidents))+
  geom_col(aes(fill=day, x=reorder(day, number_incidents)))+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title="Total number of incidents by time of day", x="Day", y="Total number of incidents by time of day")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size=rel(1.5), hjust = .5))

  1. How do the number and types of injuries compare by county? Make a table that shows the number of injury types by county. Which county has the highest number incidents? (hint: your table should be in wide format)
sharks_wide <- sharks %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  count(injury) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = "injury",
              values_from = "n")  
sharks_wide

  1. Use the table from #5 to make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by county.
sharks %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  summarize(number_incidents=n()) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=county, y=number_incidents))+
  geom_col(aes(fill=county))+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title="Total number of incidents per county", y="Total number of incidents")

  1. In the data, mode refers to a type of activity. Which activity is associated with the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  group_by(mode) %>% 
  summarize(number_incidents=n()) %>% 
  arrange(desc(number_incidents))
## # A tibble: 8 × 2
##   mode                number_incidents
##   <chr>                          <int>
## 1 Surfing / Boarding                85
## 2 Freediving                        36
## 3 Kayaking / Canoeing               30
## 4 Swimming                          22
## 5 Scuba Diving                      20
## 6 Hookah Diving                     10
## 7 Paddleboarding                     7
## 8 Walking in shallow                 1
  1. Make a plot that compares the number of incidents by activity.
sharks %>% 
  group_by(mode) %>% 
  summarize(number_incidents=n()) %>% 
  arrange(desc(number_incidents)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=mode, y=number_incidents))+
  geom_col(aes(fill=mode))+
  labs(title="Number of incidents by activity", x="Activity", y="Number of incidents")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size=rel(1.5), hjust=.5))+
  coord_flip()

  1. Which shark species is involved in the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  filter(!species=="NA") %>% 
  group_by(species) %>% 
  summarise(number_incidents=n()) %>% 
  arrange(desc(number_incidents))
## # A tibble: 11 × 2
##    species      number_incidents

##  3 Blue                        2

##  5 Leopard                     2
##  6 Salmon                      2
##  7 Blue*                       1

## 11 blue                        1
  1. Are all incidents involving Great White’s fatal? Make a plot that shows the number and types of incidents for Great White’s only.
sharks %>% 
  filter(species=="White") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=injury))+
  geom_bar(na.rm=T, aes(fill=injury))+
  labs(title="Number and types of incidents for incidents for White", x="Types of incidents for White")+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(hjust=.5))
